title: ⚠️ Broken Controls, Barely Any Co-op
body: I was excited for Monster Hunter Outlanders, but broken controls and disappointing co-op are killing my interest. Physical controller buttons frequently stop responding or trigger the wrong action. The only fix I’ve found mid-fight is getting downed, which usually happens anyway when the controls fail. That’s ridiculous for a combat-focused game. Co-op is my other major disappointment. Playing with friends is limited to short missions. I want to freely explore and hunt together, not constantly queue for another brief mission. Without meaningful improvements to controls and co-op, I won’t stick around much longer. We also need in-game button remapping and better UI customization. Especially on bigger screens, we should be able to resize, move, hide, and adjust transparency for individual interface elements and touch controls.

title: Gacha Hero Game
body: This is just another gacha hero collector. That’s it. At first you actually spend time hunting; eventually it’s just menu navigation and quick hunts (instant completion) and very little actual hunting and playing the game. There are a ton of events happening all at once for a new game; meaning new players can’t participate in a lot of them. Cause the trial versions give you no rewards and to compete you have to be level 30+. The time to complete, the FOMO psychological manipulation tactic, is very short for events too. So, this pushes you to spend. I wish I could say Capcom has a win here but this is a blemish on their reputation. All it does is make me never want to play another MH game again. MH World remains their peak MH Game. And this game is simply a copy pasta gacha with MH skin attached to it. What a disappointment. If you spend more time navigating menus and trying to figure out what it is you should be focusing on then that is a game you need to never play. It’s trying to trigger you to make an impulse buy. Capcom, you have all the money in the world and have had incredible success for the last couple of years. Why you chose to do release a gacha game, and not something that is just sub based like Pokémon does on mobile is concerning. You’re going to have nothing but whales playing and they’ll leave once they’ve exhausted what you’re offering. The game is already seeing a lot of bots which means it’s dying and not growing. No one wants this type of game anymore.

title: False enough advertising
body: You have to look past a lot as a Monster Hunter fan to enjoy this, or be a seasoned mobile gamer. The controller support and performance promised by the people they sponsored to advertise this game are poor at best. And through all of that, it’s still a gacha game so desperate for your money. As someone just trying to enjoy it like a normal game, I’m screen mirroring from IPhone 16 to a TV and connecting my controller to phone via Bluetooth (I understand screen mirroring generates some heat and uses resources). Playing reduced frame rate as even high frame rate on low gives me an overheat warning. But even the low frame rate mode is inconsistent, and baiting non-mobile gamers in with controller support, then making them do every tutorial/trial with mobile controls is just lying. “you don’t have to worry about performance on your mobile device devices. It’s been extensively optimized for performance to deliver smooth, responsive gameplay across a wide range of hardware. And yes, for those of you who don’t like touchscreen, you could just use officially supported controllers.” Exact words taken from an Outlanders ad read. I’m jumping through a lot of hoops attempting to play this game, and I realize it’s not worth it. Performance issues are partially on me due to how I’m trying to enjoy the game, controller support was misleading. I only got as far as beating Pukei-Pukei, then trying a character trial which forces you off of controller again for the hunt. So I can’t say much for the game’s content.

title: It’s good buuuuuuut-
body: To start of with, I’ve played and enjoyed monster hunter since I was in elementary school over a decade ago. I’ve gone back and played every game in the series (even the first game *shudders*). So I’d like to think I know what makes monster hunter fun or interesting through my thousands of hours across all the games. And I gotta say, I think this has done a good job so far. It has enough monster hunter DNA in it that it feels like I’m actually playing a new game in the series, and has enough new mechanics that it feels fresh and interesting. It shares most of its core gameplay with Gen 5 MH, with some things from Gen 6. I like that. Buuuuut there’s some things that are holding it back. It’d be easy to point out the obvious, such as the gacha mechanics, and how it shares a good bit of systems with say, Genshin Impact, Wuthering Waves, etc, etc. but I do understand that this is a live service game and the company wants to make money. But what truly annoys me or rather, feels most out of place, is all the other “mobile” game mechanics. Such as the weird power scaling, a billion menus and items and tutorials, the weird necessity of needing levels to get stronger and “hunter power” (I think is what they called it) that just….doesn’t really make sense? In monster hunter your power came from your gear almost exclusively (yes eating and item buffing was a thing) and that’s still here, but it only makes up for about a 1/3rd of the strength you accumulate, and I lowkey forget it’s even a thing because of how much other stuff it throws into your face. It’s almost like it’s genshin + monster hunter + afk journey (vomits). I just wish they’d remove some of the weird design choices they made that are integral for monster hunters main gameplay loop (especially the whole stamina system). Like I REALLY wanna love this game and see it’s full potential come out. But it just isn’t there yet. It’s a dang shame. I’ll still play it, as I’m in a monster hunter drought until wilds DLC drops or I replay an older title, but I am hesitant to invest heavily into it because it has those weird low grade aspects to it (which I shoulda probably went heavier into). But honestly this is basically just a schizo rant from me at this point, and I know like…a single person will probably even read this. So I’ll just stop talking now and be a bit bummed at the missed potential. Chow 👋

title: Good hunts but gacha hell
body: This one breaks my heart. I'm a long-time fan of the series, so I'm really interested in this one. I also previously played the iOS port of Freedom Unite, so I knew more or less what to hope for. Gameplay wise, this game beats my expectations and earns all highest marks. It plays well on my aging iPhone 10 Pro, it feels fast and responsive and good to play, and it communicates the core Monster Hunter experience (particularly as of World) exceptionally. Absolutely fantastic this early into release. Had it stopped there, and I were asked for the cost of a mainline game, I would be happy. But ohhhhh boy, do the wheels come off the bus once they introduce their 💸monetization💸. I'm not new to gacha games. Technically, I've played them since Puzzle Pirates, and I played both Dragalia Lost and Octopath CotC from early through end of service. So I knew what I was getting into here. The conceit of the gacha here is everything now has a power level (and eventual creep to chase), especially hunters and gear. Sure, no problem. The *problem* is there are so dang many ways to accidentally give the game your money, so many distinct gambling cutouts, and so many "deals" that they clutter out the core experience. It's as if they asked, "how do we monetize" and they decided "we will try all the things and see which stick". Because, they sure did. There's a bizarre and unnecessary energy system. Pull currencies. Gear currencies. Player leveling currencies. Event currencies. Individual gacha character currencies. And on. And on. All in their own special menus. All with daily or weekly claim buttons and bonuses. I think I stopped counting at one dozen, and all of them have "pay cash here" to boost them as distinct payments you can do. And many are very definitely pay to win. What the ever friggin' hell. It's so predatory that it makes Diablo Immortal blush. And it leaves me with enough of an awful taste that I want nothing to do with it. Anyway. This gets two stars out of me, because the game's great, it works great, but the monetization is some of the most godawful I've ever seen. Cut half of it and my review improves to 4 or 5 stars. Socksybear on MH's community team once popularly stated, to paraphrase: "We don't do microtransactions or lootboxes. See that? *points at monster* That's your lootbox." Were it still true today.

title: Review from a long time MH fan.
body: I have been playing monster hunter since Gen ultimate. I don’t know if outlanders is ment to be just a filler game but to me I feel it helps you with way too much. The zip line feature is really stupid and the auto sprint is dumb. You can just sprint yourself. So far the story is quite confusing. Long sword (the weapon it starts you with, just like in Rise.) is actually a good weapon in outlanders. The graphics are really great for a mobile game and the character creation is just as intricate as other mainline games (world, wilds, etc.) however, as far as mobile MH goes Outlanders is much much better than Monster hunter Now. ALSO, one really annoying thing that I hate about Outlanders, and I hope they get rid of it is the fact that the monster you are fighting has a damn HEALTH BAR! In no monster hunter game should there be a health bar it has never been a thing since the first game in 2004. The point of Monster hunter is you determine how weak the monster is by if it’s attacks are slower or when a little skull icon shows up on the mini map. (In rise your palico might hint that it’s weak.) Overall Monster hunter is meant to be a hardworking grinding game that you as the hunter actually have to do something in order to be good. With consistent perseverance, you can hunt elder dragons for breakfast! Monster hunter Outlanders just doesn’t give credit to such dedication because all it does is baby the hunter all the time. Thank you hope this review gives you a better understanding of MH outlanders!

title: Desperately Needs XP Sources
body: This game, overall, is really really well-made and performans nicely; it’s about what you would expect out of a MonHun game made on/for mobile. However, as the entire playerbase basically is experiencing only 48 hours into the game, there’s a ridiculously huge level cap with regard to XP for your Adventurer Rank (this game’s equivalent of Hunter Rank). XP is extremely finite, and I (along with many, many others) are basically stuck sitting at AR 25 or 26; some people managed to get up to 29. The problem is, once you’ve exhausted pretty much everything the game has to offer for XP, your ONLY sources are Daily Hunts and Daily Challenges that reward maybe about 2,000XP every 24 hours IF you keep up with it (for context, going from AR26 to 27 is about 8,000 or so XP; so, four DAYS to go up by one level IF all goes well). The apparent AR cap is 60, but with where everyone is right now there’s still about 60% of the game locked away behind a time gate (or a huge money sink) for pretty much no good reason. With that, there is one super-super easy fix the devs can implement: After AR20 let Free Hunts and Field Hunts award AR XP. Frees can award 100XP, and Fields can award 50XP. Easy. We already get 100RP (Research Points) for Capturing monsters; why not give AR XP for killing inversely? This would still allow players to progress, while still incentivizing the “pay to progress/win” aspect this game inevitably has (because it’s free to play) with a grind (a slow grind is better than no grind). As is, once you’ve exhausted all your XP sources for the day, there’s almost no reason to continue playing for most people; no consistent playerbase means no money.

An average hunt is 1-4 minutes based on skill, which can be nice and rewarding when you want to engage with story or get strong fast. It’s not a cheap port, it’s made from the ground up for mobile, with an amazing graphics engine, lots of unique animations, pre rendered and real time cutscenes from the engine, awesome textures like wet mud on mud creatures. Very impressive game, I’m gonna have to play the PS5 monster hunter after I’m done with all chapters in this. It’s now my defacto game to play until GTA VI.
